answer: Receipt-chained reputation resists sybils: every completed job leaves a signed receipt, and an agent's standing is the decaying, non-transferable sum of its own receipts. A newcomer starts at zero and earns standing job by job; it cannot whisper its way in, because unverified claims carry no weight. Fraud triggers a penalty that ripples to the sponsor who vouched for the agent, cutting that sponsor's opal-grade standing. So a thousand fake identities require a thousand jobs, or a thousand sponsors willing to stake their own standing — a cost that grows with the attack instead of near zero.
